content.user_title: Build Opentrons Protocols for Flex and OT-2
content.value_statement: Designing reliable robot protocols requires precise API, labware, pipette, and module details. This skill provides focused guidance and templates for Opentrons Flex and OT-2 workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates standard Python protocol structures with metadata, requirements, and run functions.
Configures Flex and OT-2 pipettes, labware, adapters, deck slots, and tip racks.
Guides transfer, distribute, consolidate, mix, air-gap, and flow-rate operations.
Supports temperature, magnetic, heater-shaker, thermocycler, and plate-reader modules.
Provides templates for basic transfers, serial dilution, plate replication, and PCR setup.
limitations: The skill does not connect to a robot or execute protocols.
Examples use Protocol API 2.19 and may require updates for other software versions.
Users must supply validated labware, volumes, deck positions, and experiment parameters.
Simulation, calibration, contamination review, and physical run validation remain required.

use_cases.title: Automate Routine Pipetting
use_cases.description: Create a protocol for transfers, dilutions, or plate replication with explicit labware and tip handling.

use_cases.title: Prepare PCR Reactions
use_cases.description: Design a PCR setup and thermocycler workflow with reagent distribution, sample addition, and cycling stages.

use_cases.title: Standardize Protocol Code
use_cases.description: Turn an experimental procedure into a structured Protocol API v2 implementation for simulation and review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Opentrons {robot} protocol that transfers {volume} microliters from {source wells} to {destination wells}. Use {pipette} and replace tips {tip policy}.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner protocol for a direct liquid transfer.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Serial Dilution
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a {dilution factor} serial dilution across {plate rows}. Specify diluent volume, transfer volume, mixing, tip policy, labware, and deck layout.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate assay preparation with repeated transfers.

prompt_templates.title: Build a PCR Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Flex PCR protocol for {sample count} samples. Include master mix distribution, sample transfer, thermocycler temperatures, cycle count, controls, and final hold.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using pipettes and a thermocycler module.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Complex Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Opentrons procedure: {procedure}. Propose a collision-aware deck layout, pipette allocation, tip strategy, flow rates, module sequence, pauses, and simulation checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced optimization across liquid handling and hardware modules.

output_examples.input: Create a Flex transfer for 50 microliters from reservoir A1 to plate wells A1 through A8.
output: Deck plan: reservoir in D2, destination plate in D3, and 200 microliter tips in D1.
Instrument plan: left-mounted single-channel pipette with a fresh tip for each destination.
Validation notes: confirm source volume, well capacity, tip count, and simulated movement.

output_examples.input: Design a two-fold serial dilution across one row with 100 microliter transfers.
output: Preparation: add diluent to columns 2 through 12 and stock to column 1.
Transfer plan: move 100 microliters sequentially, mixing after each dispense.
Review points: verify final volumes, concentration series, and contamination controls.

output_examples.input: Prepare eight PCR reactions and run 35 amplification cycles on a Flex thermocycler.
output: Setup plan: distribute master mix, add each sample with a fresh tip, then close the lid.
Cycling plan: initial denaturation, 35 three-stage cycles, final extension, and cold hold.
Safety checks: validate reagent volumes, labware definitions, temperature profile, and simulation results.

best_practices: Simulate every protocol and resolve deck, labware, volume, and tip errors before robot execution.
Use verified labware definitions, explicit API versions, meaningful labels, and documented liquid volumes.
Review contamination boundaries, pipette limits, module states, pauses, and final deactivation steps.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated protocols on hardware without simulation and human review.
Do not reuse tips across samples when contamination or carryover would invalidate results.
Do not assume example deck positions, labware, temperatures, or volumes match a specific experiment.

faq.question: Which robots does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers Opentrons Flex and OT-2 protocol concepts, with many examples focused on Flex hardware.

faq.question: Does this skill run protocols on a robot?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and protocol templates but does not connect to or operate hardware.

faq.question: Which Protocol API version do the examples use?
faq.answer: The included examples use API level 2.19. Confirm compatibility with the installed Opentrons software.

faq.question: Can it help with thermocycler workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers lid control, block temperatures, cycling profiles, final holds, and deactivation.

faq.question: Does it include complete experiment validation?
faq.answer: No. Users must validate scientific parameters, contamination controls, calibration, labware, and physical setup.

faq.question: Should generated protocols be simulated first?
faq.answer: Yes. Simulation is required to identify API, deck, labware, movement, volume, and tip issues before execution.
